verdict.rationale: npm's own docs say the client can be pointed at any compatible registry, including one you run yourself, and can install from a new registry after switching. The evidence shows no first-party, self-hostable npm registry server, so the actual server would be a third-party tool like Verdaccio, which earns no credit. missing for 10: first-party self-hostable registry software, self-hosting deployment docs, independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted setup.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: You can configure npm to use any compatible registry you like, and even run your own registry.
you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
